utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, to everyone in and just around the courtroom assisting us. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. For the continuation of the cross-examination of the witness, we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Are there any procedural matters to be raised? We dealt with most of them quite recently. Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I see that the Defence is also -- remains seated, both Defence teams, therefore if there are no further procedural issues we will adjourn. And as explained earlier, and also the reasons why we will not have any hearings next week, then there is the decision of the Chamber on the motion for an adjournment which keeps us out of court for a couple of weeks, but early April we have no court schedule yet, so I can't give you the precise date on which we will resume. The parties will be informed about it as soon as possible. That's, of course, the first week after the weeks the Chamber indicated we would not sit, but whether that would be a Monday, Tuesday, or any other days of that week is still uncertain. Therefore, adjournment will be sine die, without a day set. Any other matters at this moment? Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask the Court if the Court could give us an indication when it would decide on the motion for filing the questions with Dr. Eekhof in light of our provisional release application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we received the new questions late yesterday afternoon, and since all the judges were busy with other matters this morning, we have not found time yet. If there would be -- of course, the first is the Chamber will look at the questions, see whether these questions are appropriately put to the Dr. Eekhof or whether the Chamber itself will rephrase one or more of these questions, then we have to wait for the answer of Dr. Eekhof. And once we've received the answers, we will have to decide whether we want to have any further information from Dr. Eekhof in a hearing, and this, of course, all to prepare a decision on provisional release. I can't give you at this moment any further indications apart from that the Chamber is aware of the urgency of the matter, and the Chamber will not lose unnecessarily time to decide the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you will allow me a few words. As you know, we have submitted a request of provisional release of Mr. Simatovic with the appropriate guarantees provided by the Government of the Republic of Serbia. I believe and I still trust that we have very good a collegiate relations with the OTP, but I would now ask the OTP to just, if they can, speed up with their reply to our request, and I am not addressing the Trial Chamber with the request to actually issue an order to that effect to the OTP, but, rather, I am appealing to the OTP to request that they provide their answer as soon as they can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before we even considering an order, we will first hear what the Prosecution has to offer in respect of timing of their response. Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the parties have been informed, Mr. Groome at that point in time is on official business, but he returns tomorrow. We have been working on the draft, and we intend to file it by the end of the week. So within a week from the official filing. I would like to add if the Chamber further considers to limit that time further, that in our view the motions of -- hasn't been filed urgent. It was known since the 19th of February that there would be an adjournment, and the filing was only submitted on last Friday, late afternoon, while we were all sitting in court. Since then we have been again in court for two days, which is partly why we are still considering the response on the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome informed Chamber staff that we could expect a response to be filed tomorrow. So therefore -- yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but I feel bound to reply to Mr. Hoffmann. He is absolutely correct, and it is this Defence team's error. We were not sure as to what was going to happen with the 18th and 19th, whether we were going to work on those days or not, and, of course, we could have submitted our request to be effective as of the moment of the delay, and on. And of course it was an error on our part, but I appealed to the Trial Chamber and the OTP to have understanding for our position, because the whole point of this delay of the proceedings was to allow us to have some additional time to work with our accused because he is the most appropriate person who can assist us in the preparation of his Defence, and I do acknowledge that it was our mistake in filing this just last Friday, but that was simply because we weren't counting on this time as being counted, the delayed time as being counted from now onwards and not from after the 19th. And we apologise for filing our request too late, and we would very much appreciate if the Prosecution could reply by tomorrow. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I certainly stand corrected. If that information was provided that we will file tomorrow, we will do so by the end of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I rely on the very specific information in relation to this; whereas it seems that your announcement that you would reply by Friday was a bit on the basis that you would wait for Mr. Groome to return and then to further discuss the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to give both parties a bit, the Chamber would appreciate to receive the response by tomorrow close of business, but orders it to be filed not later than Thursday, the 11th, at noon, which gives you at least a night and a morning to further have a better -- with Mr. Groome, Mr. Hoffmann, if there is any need. Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is our understanding that Prosecution still intends to file questions for Dr. Eekhof as well if the Court grants our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We haven't seen anything. Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I was about to raise earlier on and to indicate to the parties and the Chambers that we have prepared that, and as soon as we get out of court we will file that and also provide the courtesy copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we can -- which allows us to consider all the questions together. And so that will be filed today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Right after court, and we will make sure that we send out courtesy copies directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood. The Chamber appreciates the flexibility shown by the parties in this respect. I would say in this respect, obviously, and primarily, the Prosecution. Any other matter to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing. Then we adjourn, as I explained and announced earlier, sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5.03 p.m. sine die. 24 25
